output.title: Measure list hygiene before you automate it
output.body:
If you want to measure list hygiene, make it a bounded workflow decision, not a vague “clean up the list” project. Pick one visible problem first: bounce rate, complaint rate, or falling engagement. Then decide what action that metric would trigger. If the answer is “not much,” you are probably measuring for comfort, not control.

For a small business, the first pass usually does not need AI. Bounce counts, unsubscribe trends, and complaint feedback are rule-based signals. Your existing email tool probably already has some reporting, and a simple pivot table can do the rest. AI only becomes relevant if you need help classifying complaint reasons, spotting patterns in older feedback, or grouping contacts by engagement. That is a separate task from measuring list hygiene itself.

A useful diagnostic question is: “What would I do differently if I knew this list was getting worse?” If the answer is concrete — remove bounces, pause a re-engagement send, suppress a segment — then the metric has a job. If the answer is vague, the metric is just a dashboard ornament. Nice to look at, not very helpful.

Practical next step: export your current list report, note one threshold you would actually act on, and write the action beside it. Keep the threshold simple and review whether the data enters the decision before you think about automation. Measurement without a decision is just tidying the spreadsheet.
